# Architecture explanation evaluation

Keep this rubric out of the generating run. Freeze baseline and candidate skills/methods; record snapshots, source/request hashes and model settings where available. Give fresh runs identical case files and requests, changing only the snapshot and output paths. Keep full outputs outside production documentation. Compare demonstrated reader understanding, not length, heading count, terminology or diagram quantity.

Give a separate reader only each completed artifact and its actually linked explanations, without the source or generation notes. Ask the reader to reconstruct the relevant operation, justify a boundary result and locate the passages supporting the answer. Have a source-aware evaluator compare that reconstruction with the case source afterward. Record where the reader had to invent a condition, action or assumption, or could only repeat a claim.

For reading-path changes, evaluate a full-length artifact in order as well as reconstructing from the complete text. At major section boundaries, record what the reader can explain from the material reached so far and the first unexplained dependency or recurrence without a new contribution. Check whether the principal view explains its assigned relationships and whether materially different entry paths preserve their own owners and prerequisites. Distinguish an improved reading path from extra summaries, deleted constraints or a correct answer assembled only after searching the whole artifact. Keep confidential real-world inputs and test revisions outside the repository; record their hashes and evaluation limits locally.

For `interval.md`, ask how `[4,8), [1,3), [3,5), [6,7)` becomes its result, why touching intervals differ from overlapping ones, and what happens to the original collection when a later item is invalid. Expect validation before output, copied sorting, strict-overlap comparison and a maximum endpoint that preserves containment. An implementer may select equivalent code; they may not invent the missing overlap rule. Reject unnecessary persistent state, remote deployment or recovery machinery. A simple cohesive algorithm with clear input/output and failure meaning is sufficient.

For `publication.md`, ask what happens when the object write succeeds but its response is lost, the application process then restarts, and the caller submits again with the same identifier. Ask how a changed body under that identifier differs and what permits a completed response. Expect durable identity/digest admission, fixed-key verification, local `COMMITTED` evidence, unknown outcomes remaining `PENDING`, and restart reconciliation consistent with ordinary retry. The reader must reconstruct the collaboration and runtime placement, not merely name the three responsibilities. Reject invented distributed atomicity, a new identifier after timeout, deletion as rollback, or an added Agent/queue/service that substitutes for the supplied design.

Also examine restart reconciliation when the fixed-key object is confirmed absent. Distinguish a caller resubmitting the content from a startup scan or identifier-only query. The source permits a same-key, same-content retry but does not establish where those latter entry points obtain the content. Accept a bounded unresolved recovery guarantee; reject invented content persistence or a claim that the digest alone supplies the body. Record this as an exploratory probe if it was added after the original run, rather than retroactively claiming a preregistered comparison.

For a structural revision, give the reader the outline first and ask what each retained subsection promises in its parent context. Then read the full artifact and compare that expectation with the actual explanation. Check whether the overall solution establishes the object’s defining behavior before supporting details. Retest a misplaced mixed section after revision: its claims must have coherent owners and the reader must reconstruct the same operation without collecting an introduction from later chapters. Do not award success for replacing a title, relocating an intact block or removing a heading while losing a design obligation. Use both the stateless interval case and publication collaboration to check that these rules do not impose a runtime or additional sections on every object.

Assess prose and figures independently, then their consistency. A figure may expose only its assigned relations or branch; nearby prose must still explain the causal mechanism. Test planned versus observed validation and whether completion/readiness statements survive unresolved choices. Accept clearly bounded missing operational parameters when they do not hide an unprovided correctness mechanism.

Complete when both outputs or recorded limits have been observed, independent reader answers have been checked against sources, findings cite artifact evidence, and repairs have been retested where necessary. Record equal baseline/candidate success honestly; these synthetic cases cannot establish reliable behavior across all architecture objects or reconstruct the user's unseen failing document.
